evidence: Lewis & Short: Histrum fluvium (Naev.), illum locum (Cic.)
terms.comment: Transitive: the river or place one lives beside is the object (Nīlum accolere), and in the passive the river is the subject: fluvius crēbrīs oppidīs accolitur (Plin. NH 3.9, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: amnis accolitur dextrā laevāque crēbrīs oppidīs
phrases.english: the river is dotted with towns on both banks

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
